questions.q: What does an "open receivable" actually represent?
options: Cash already sitting in the company's bank account
A cancelled transaction
A legal and accounting claim to future cash that hasn't arrived yet
A discount applied to an order
questions.explain: An open receivable is a claim that the customer owes money — not cash in hand.

questions.q: What is "aging," in the context of a Receivables invoice?
options: How long an invoice has been outstanding relative to its due date
How old the item being sold is
The number of lines on the invoice
The customer's years as a client
questions.explain: Aging tracks how long an invoice has been open relative to its due date, using buckets like current, 1-30 days past due, etc.

questions.q: What is SO-48217's open balance after the credit memo, and its terms?
options: $58,000.00, Due on receipt
questions.explain: After the $2,755.00 credit memo, the invoice balance is $52,345.00, due Net 30.

questions.q: What must happen for SO-48217's receivable to actually close?
options: Nothing — it closes automatically after 30 days regardless of payment
A cash receipt for the open amount must arrive and be applied specifically to this invoice
The order must be re-submitted
A new credit check must run
questions.explain: The receivable only closes when a matching cash receipt arrives and is applied to this specific invoice.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say "the invoice is not the finish line" for Order-to-Cash?
options: Because invoices are frequently cancelled
Because invoices never get paid
Because there is a real gap between recognizing the sale/billing it and actually receiving the cash
Because the invoice has no accounting impact
questions.explain: Revenue is recognized and the inventory is already gone at invoicing, but the cash itself is still pending until it's collected.
